subject: Follow-up: Hyperscaler trial gaps & prioritized A/B bench plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@hyperscaler.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Hyperscaler trial gaps & prioritized A/B bench plan

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Key discovery notes
- Your team needs stable p95 < 120ms for short-chat scenarios and p99 < 400ms for long form (8-12k tokens).
- Nebula is running a mix of synchronous low-latency and batch-heavy throughput workloads (peak 10k tokens/sec across 8k concurrent users).
- Security: SOC 2 + isolated networking are blockers for procurement; you flagged private deployment as a must-have for production.

2) Where the hyperscaler trial left gaps (what you asked us to help validate)
- Our initial side-by-side (hosted) shows Redwood p95 ~ 95ms vs Hyperscaler p95 ~ 140ms on the 2k token reference, p99: Redwood 360ms vs Hyperscaler 520ms (see attached summary).
- Throughput: Redwood sustained 3.4k tokens/sec on a standard config vs Hyperscaler 2.1k tokens/sec under the same simulated load (tokens/sec measured at stable tail execution).
- Failure modes: hyperscaler showed memory pressure spikes with long-seq KV cache turn-on; we suggest targeted A/B to reproduce and triage.

3) Proposed immediate A/B bench plan (priority + owners)
- A/B Test A (short-chat latency): Run 50k requests, 2k token cap, p95/p99 measurement across 3 regions — owner: Marissa (week of 10/9).
- A/B Test B (long seq throughput): Simulate 8k-token sessions, peak 10k tokens/sec synthetic load, record sustained tokens/sec and tail p99 — owner: Rafael (run 10/10–10/12).
- A/B Test C (KV cache enabled): Run long-seq with cold/warm cache passes to surface memory spikes — owner: Jonas (instrument with perf-trace on 10/11).

4) Ask from Nebula
- Procurement: target timeline for Private deployment checklist and SOC 2 artifacts. Beth requested MFA/Audit log extracts.

Next steps: I attached a short CSV with our quick baseline numbers and a mutual action plan doc. Can you confirm Beth and your infra lead (name/email) to include in the next tech sync? If we get a green light we’ll schedule the first A/B (short-chat) next Monday morning.

Cheers,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-latency-summary.csv (CSV, 26KB), mutual-action-plan.docx (DOCX, 18KB)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@hyperscaler.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Beth Procure <beth.procure@nebula-cloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 06 Oct 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Hyperscaler trial gaps & prioritized A/B bench plan

Jonas — appreciate the fast recap and the numbers. A couple quick notes from our side: 

- The p95/p99 deltas you pasted are consistent with what we saw in our internal run, but we want to validate under Nebula's real traffic shape (bursty, high prefix-reuse).
- I'll loop in our infra lead (Samir Patel) — Samir@hyperscaler.ai — for the tech sync. He'll also share the telemetry we used for the trial.
- Procurement: Beth asked for a clear artifact list; I can push SOC 2 + KMS integration notes this week.

Agree with the proposed A/Bs. Can we compress the short-chat A/B to run overnight on Sunday (10/8) as a pre-check? If Redwood can provide a runnable perf harness (k6/locust scenario) plus the config snippets, Samir can mirror them on our side.

On timelines: if the short-chat A/B shows <10% delta at p95, Nebula is comfortable moving to a narrow pilot for a week. If >10%, they'll request deeper triage and possibly a combined quantization/infra tweak.

—Alex
Alex Turner
Solutions Engineer — Hyperscaler AI
alex.turner@hyperscaler.ai

Date: Mon, 08 Oct 2028 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Hyperscaler trial gaps & prioritized A/B bench plan

Thanks — I started the short-chat A/B harness last night (Sunday run) and attached a small sanity plot to the Drive link. Quick observations:

- Baseline (hosted): p95 = 98ms, p99 = 375ms (matches Jonas's numbers within sampling noise).
- Hyperscaler mirror: p95 = 135ms, p99 = 510ms. Hyperscaler run showed a 12% higher p95 for short-chat and ~36% worse p99.
- CPU scheduling: we saw increased context switches at ~85% utilization on Hyperscaler nodes; looks like the kernel scheduler plus a different kernel build is impacting tail. Rafael is digging into perf traces to confirm.

Rafael — can you prep the long-seq harness and we'll align on instrumentation (perf counters + kv cache traces)? I put owners into the MAP doc.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment stub: short-chat-sanity-plot.png (PNG, 42KB)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@hyperscaler.ai>, Beth Procure <beth.procure@nebula-cloud.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Hyperscaler trial gaps & prioritized A/B bench plan

Looping back with the plan and a couple of concrete test definitions (summary below). I scheduled the long-seq run for 10/10 09:00 PT and the KV cache runs for 10/11 09:00 PT. Links to results will be posted to the Drive link after each run.

Test definitions (short):
- Short-chat A/B (owner: Marissa): 100k requests, 2k token cap, 95/99 percentiles, 3 regions (us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1). Baseline run completed.
- Long-seq throughput (owner: Rafael): 8k token sessions, 40s median tail generation window, step-up to peak 10k tokens/sec sustained for 60s, measure sustained tokens/sec and p99. Instrumentation: per-request KV cache hit ratio, memory/alloc graphs, OS-level sched stats.
- KV warm/cold (owner: Jonas): run 50 warm passes, 10 cold passes, capture GC and per-layer memory.

Deliverables and timelines:
- 10/10 EOD: long-seq run results + csv (measured tokens/sec, p95/p99, memory traces).
- 10/12 EOD: consolidated A/B summary and recommended mitigations (quantization profiles / kernel tweaks / routing policy).

Beth — for procurement, I attached a checklist and will share the SOC 2 snapshot after Alex pushes his artifacts. If Nebula wants, we can run a Private PoC in a dedicated VLAN to eliminate noisy neighbor risk — estimate 2 weeks to provision once the PO is in.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Performance Engineering Lead — Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
